arxiv-2104-08669.creator: Alan Edelman, Sungwoo Jeong
arxiv-2104-08669.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alan Edelman, Sungwoo Jeong. The success of matrix factorizations such as the singular value decomposition (SVD) has motivated the search for even more factorizations. We catalog 53 matrix factorizations, most of which we believe to be new.

arxiv-2208-14854.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ashley Clayton & Nik Ruškuc. In 1981/82, Hickin & Plotkin and McKenzie both proved that a finite group has only countably many non-isomorphic subdirect powers if and only if it is abelian. In this paper, we prove that a finite commutative semigroup has only countably many non-isomorphic countable subdirect powers if and only if it is either a finite abelian group or a null semigroup. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification

arxiv-2209-02382.title: Higher-order corrections to the spin-orbit and spin-spin tensor interactions in HD +
arxiv-2209-02382.creator: Mohammad Haidar 1 , Vladimir I. Korobov 2 , Laurent Hilico 1,3 , and Jean-Philippe Karr 1,3
arxiv-2209-02382.description: Abstract Improved values of hyperfine coefficients related to the electronic spin-orbit and electron-nucleus spin-spin tensor interactions in the HD + molecular ion are obtained through numerical calculation of relativistic corrections at the m ​ α 6 m\alpha^{6} order and radiative corrections at the m ​ α 7 ​ ln ⁡ ( α ) m\alpha^{7}\ln(\alpha) order.

arxiv-2301-08640.title: Tracing the Evolution of SMBHs and Stellar Objects in Galaxy Mergers: An Multi-mass Direct N -body Model
arxiv-2301-08640.creator: Shuo Li, Shiyan Zhong, Peter Berczik, Rainer Spurzem, Xian Chen, F.K. Liu
arxiv-2301-08640.description: Abstract By using direct N -body numerical simulations, we model the dynamical co-evolution of two supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and the surrounding stars in merging galaxies. In order to investigate how different stellar components evolve during the merger, we generate evolved stellar distributions with an initial mass function.

arxiv-2307-05902.title: Stability Guarantees for Feature Attributions with Multiplicative Smoothing
arxiv-2307-05902.creator: Anton Xue, Rajeev Alur, Eric Wong
arxiv-2307-05902.description: Abstract Explanation methods for machine learning models tend not to provide any formal guarantees and may not reflect the underlying decision-making process. In this work, we analyze stability as a property for reliable feature attribution methods. We prove that relaxed variants of stability are guaranteed if the model is sufficiently Lipschitz with respect to the masking of features.

arxiv-2402-03212.title: Angular Momentum Transport in Binary Star Formation: The Enhancement of Magneto-Rotational Instability and Role of Outflows SFUMATO ( Matsumoto 2007 ) , Paraview
arxiv-2402-03212.creator: Tomoaki Matsumoto
arxiv-2402-03212.description: Abstract The formation of binary stars is highly influenced by magnetic fields, which play a crucial role in transporting angular momentum. We conducted three-dimensional numerical simulations of binary star accretion via a circumbinary disk, taking into account a magnetic field perpendicular to the disk and an infalling envelope.

arxiv-2402-10241.title: Quantum Tunneling Insights into the Atomic Landscapes of Graphite, Gold, and Silicon
arxiv-2402-10241.creator: Dhananjay Saikumar
arxiv-2402-10241.description: Abstract Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) is a powerful technique that utilizes quantum tunneling to visualize atomic surfaces with high precision. This study presents detailed topographic maps and evaluates the local density of states (LDOS) for three distinct materials: Highly Oriented Pyrolytic Graphite (HOPG), gold, and silicon.

arxiv-2412-01363.title: Exploring the Robustness of AI-Driven Tools in Digital Forensics: A Preliminary Study Journal: Digital Forensics Research Conference Europe 2025
arxiv-2412-01363.creator: Silvia Lucia Sanna, Leonardo Regano, Davide Maiorca, Giorgio Giacinto
arxiv-2412-01363.description: Abstract Nowadays, many tools are used to facilitate forensic tasks about data extraction and data analysis. In particular, some tools leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) to automatically label examined data into specific categories (i.e., drugs, weapons, nudity). However, this raises a serious concern about the robustness of the employed AI algorithms against adversarial attacks.

arxiv-2505-12605.title: Temporal-Oriented Recipe for Transferring Large Vision-Language Model to Video Understanding
arxiv-2505-12605.creator: Thong Nguyen Zhiyuan Hu Xu Lin, Cong-Duy Nguyen See-Kiong Ng Luu Anh Tuan
arxiv-2505-12605.description: Abstract Recent years have witnessed outstanding advances of large vision-language models (LVLMs). In order to tackle video understanding, most of them depend upon their implicit temporal understanding capacity. As such, they have not deciphered important components that contribute to temporal understanding ability, which might limit the potential of these LVLMs for video understanding.

pmc-12386544.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Neuromodulation in Heart Failure with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fraction: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Future Directions
pmc-12386544.creator: Rabiah Aslam Ansari, Sidhartha Gautam Senapati, Vibhor Ahluwalia, Gianeshwaree Alias Rachna Panjwani, Anmolpreet Kaur, Gayathri Yerrapragada, Jayavinamika Jayapradhaban Kala, Poonguzhali Elangovan, Shiva Sankari Karuppiah, Naghmeh Asadimanesh, Anjani Muthyala, Shivaram P Arunachalam, Imo A Ebong
pmc-12386544.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Heart failure, a significant global health burden, is divided into heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), characterized by systolic dysfunction and diastolic stiffness, respectively. While HFrEF benefits from pharmacological and device-based therapies, HFpEF lacks effective treatments, with both conditions leading to high rehospitalization rates and reduced quality of life, especially in older adults with comorbidities. This review explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in advancing autonomic neuromodulation for heart failure management.

pmc-12701637.title: Therapeutic Outcomes of Shelf-Stable, Cryopreserved Amniotic Membrane in Recalcitrant Keratopathy
pmc-12701637.creator: Milanka Stevanovic, Gina Ciarmiello, Robert Eden, Robert Schultze
pmc-12701637.description: PurposeKeratopathy can be caused by multiple factors including neuropathy, inflammation, radiation, among others. Amniotic membrane (AM) is known to have anti-inflammatory and anti-scarring properties, which helps promote epithelialization. Herein, we assessed application of AM to promote epithelialization in the treatment of recalcitrant keratopathy.

pmc-13190764.title: Coupling observational methods and the DayCent model to improve examinations of N2O production pathways
pmc-13190764.creator: Shauna-kay Rainford, Julius C Havsteen, Joachim Mohn, Christof Ammann, Sonja G Keel
pmc-13190764.description: The traditional calibration approach for process-based models, such as DayCent, consists of the iterative adjustment of model parameters and comparison of the simulated total N2O flux to measured observations. However, the contributions of individual production pathways, namely nitrification and denitrification, are uncertain.

pmc-13283628.title: Association Between Auditory Profile Symptom Burden and Balance Dysfunction in Pediatric Patients with Persistent Post-Concussive Symptoms
pmc-13283628.creator: Joseph Marshall, Luke Muratalla Maes, Amal Anilkumar, Aditya Rohilla, Aparna Chandrasekar, Kyle Kener, Ajuni Choudhary, Leslie Streeter, Jaden Bailey, James Dill, Leila Samsam, Leah Gawin, Brett Dusenberry, Anthony Gross, Mo Mortazavi
pmc-13283628.description: Background:Persistent post-concussive symptoms (PPCS) can affect various functional domains in pediatric patients, including balance and sensory processing. Auditory symptom burden, such as sound sensitivity or difficulty filtering noises, is increasingly recognized in PPCS, but its relationship to objective measures of postural stability remains underexplored. Force plate sway velocity (FPSV) offers a quantifiable assessment of balance and vestibular function.

pmc-13391992.title: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound versus CT angiography for endoleak detection after EVAR: a reference-standard-aware systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13391992.creator: Rafaella Brandão de Melo Soares, Rafael de Negreiros Botan, Iruena Moraes Kessler
pmc-13391992.description: PurposeTo evaluate contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) for endoleak detection after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) against CT angiography (CTA) or CTA-centered composite references, explicitly treating CTA as an imperfect reference standard.MethodsWe searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, Crossref, OpenAlex, and performed an institutional Embase/Scopus coverage audit through 13 May 2026, with citation checking from prior reviews and included-study bibliographies.

pmc-13395071.title: Iatrogenic large coronary artery fistula treated with coronary artery stenting in an 8-year-old child: a case report
pmc-13395071.creator: Sidra Yoosannaf, Masood Sadiq, Ahmad Usaid Qureshi, Muhammad Muzaffar Mahmood
pmc-13395071.description: BackgroundIatrogenic coronary artery fistula, although a rare complication after cardiac surgery, may lead to haemodynamic instability and requires immediate recognition and management. Percutaneous coronary intervention despite its technical challenges is a viable intervention in selected paediatric cases.Case SummaryWe report a case of an 8-year-old child who had cardiac surgery for TOF with pulmonary atresia.

pmc-13581810.title: The effectiveness of the intervention model based on cognitive behavioral therapy in reducing risky sexual behaviors among MSM
pmc-13581810.creator: Xiaochen Xiang, Xiaobing Zhai, Yumeng Lei, Jialu Feng, Qiang Wang
pmc-13581810.description: MethodsBased on CBT theory and the Internet, we established an intervention model targeting high-risk sexual behavior patterns in MSM. We then conducted a randomized controlled trial (n = 50) to assess the impact of the CBT-based intervention on high-risk sexual behaviors and gut microbiota changes in this population.

pmc-13589612.title: FIRM‐P separates knee phenotype from patient context in anterior cruciate ligament‐related instability: A conceptual framework integrating arthrogenic muscle inhibition as a cross‐domain modifier
pmc-13589612.creator: Dario Giunchi, Matteo Denti, Marc Barrera Uso
pmc-13589612.description: PurposeClinical reasoning after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury is still often built on isolated proxies such as imaging, instrumented laxity, functional testing or patient‐reported instability. These variables are clinically useful, but they are not interchangeable and do not answer the same question.

pmc-13679841.title: Neointimal Hyperplasia and Restenosis: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology, Animal Models, Clinical Features, Diagnosis, and Management
pmc-13679841.creator: Kaixu Wang, Daiyu Zhang, Yu Hu, Yixin Zhao, Xinling Wang, Long Jiang, Meixiu Jiang
pmc-13679841.description: In‐stent restenosis (ISR) remains a major complication following vascular interventions, with neointimal hyperplasia representing a central pathological process that can adversely affect postoperative outcomes. Accumulating evidence indicates that neointimal hyperplasia is driven by vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic transition, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and multiple forms of programmed cell death. Despite substantial advances, the underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain incompletely understood.
